content.title: About
content.content: Doughnut holes are small, round pieces of dough made from the same yeasted or cake batter as regular doughnuts. They are typically deep‑fried until golden and finished with powdered sugar, glaze, or sprinkles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Often called “donut holes” because they look like the missing center of a traditional doughnut.
In the United States they are a popular snack at fairs and coffee shops, sometimes called “mini‑donuts.”
Both sweet and savory versions exist; savory batches are flavored with spices such as cinnamon and nutmeg.
In some countries they are used as a base for dessert salads mixed with fruit and whipped cream.
Their bite‑size shape makes them easy to pack in single‑serve bags, a favorite among kids.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides quick‑digesting carbohydrates that replenish muscle glycogen.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: The wheat‑based dough supplies a modest amount of plant protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeasted dough is a source of B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides small amounts of iron, magnesium, and phosphorus.

items.title: Mood‑boosting pleasure
items.content: Sweet taste can trigger endorphin release, improving mood temporarily.

items.title: High sugar and fat content
items.content: Frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain and elevated blood sugar levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Made with wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Trans fats from frying
items.content: Using reused oil can introduce trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Burn risk
items.content: When frying at home, handle hot oil carefully to avoid burns.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve doughnut holes warm, dusted with powdered sugar, glaze, cinnamon, or chocolate. They pair well with berry sauce, ice cream, or can be layered in dessert parfaits.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate up to a week or freeze for up to 3 months.
